title: The Wolf of Highmoor
premise: Marguerite Delacroix has spent her life as the last Warden of Highmoor, tending a gate in the valley where magic cannot follow, believing the war it once unleashed is long dead. When a child arrives speaking the tongue of the old kingdoms, she learns the gate is not sealed but starving, and that the usurper's armies march to claim what leaks through it. As soldiers close on the free cities, Marguerite must choose between destroying the gate and losing every memory of the people she loves, or opening it and risking the ancient war's return. In the end she feeds the gate her own past, sealing it forever at the cost of forgetting why she ever stayed.
about_author: Yara Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charters before turning to fantasy. She writes from a farmhouse in the northern hills, where she claims the fog does most of the plotting.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She makes her seasonal rounds of the gate beneath Highmoor, checking wards that hum with a silence she has never questioned. We learn the valley eats magic, and that she inherited the wardenship from a mother whose face she can barely recall. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A boy of perhaps eight appears at her cottage in a snowstorm, speaking a language older than any kingdom, unafraid of the valley's dead air. He calls the mountain by its true name, which no living person should know. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with the boy Tam listening. Descending to the gate, she finds the wards frayed and hears, for the first time, whispers pressing through from the other side. The child translates: they are calling someone home. Emotional beat: the keeper realizes she is the prisoner, not the guard.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Herald
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Captain Aldric Vane, scouting the valley for the usurper's army, carrying orders to find the 'door that dreams.' His men sicken near the wards; he alone feels drawn to them. Emotional beat: ambition shadowed by an unease he cannot name.

chapters.title: Tam's True Name
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Tam confesses he came through the gate; he is what leaked out when the wards weakened, a fragment given flesh. If the gate opens fully, everything on the other side follows him back. Emotional beat: tenderness for the child warring with horror at what he is.

chapters.title: Soldiers in the Pass
chapters.summary: Alternating Marguerite and Aldric POVs. Vane's company reaches the valley; skirmishes with free-city scouts spill blood on ward-stones, and each drop strengthens the gate's pull. Marguerite shelters refugees who bring news: the free cities will fall within a season. Emotional beat: the outside world arrives, and it is worse than feared.

chapters.title: The Price of the Ward
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her mother's journal reveals the truth: the gate is fed by memory, and every Warden before her paid in recollections until nothing remained but duty. Marguerite tests it, sacrificing one memory, and watches the wards blaze bright. Emotional beat: grief as currency.

chapters.title: The Breaking of Highmoor
chapters.summary: Climax, all POVs converging. Vane seizes the gate chamber, forcing Marguerite to open it at sword-point; Tam stands between them as the seal fractures and the first of the old powers presses through. Marguerite turns the gate's hunger on itself, offering everything she is. Emotional beat: sacrifice at the edge of annihilation.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, fragmented. The gate closes, fed by her memories of her mother, her years, her reasons. She wakes in the cottage knowing only that a boy needs her and a mountain must be watched. Vane, broken by what he saw, refuses to report the valley exists. Emotional beat: survival without selfhood.

chapters.title: Spring at the Edge of the Map
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Snow melts; refugees settle in the valley, safe because magic cannot follow them here. Tam tends Marguerite, teaching her small new memories to replace the stolen ones, and keeps the old language alive so the gate's silence holds. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal—the price was paid, and life continues anyway.
